Not accurate
body: As a user who relies on accurate and consistent blood pressure readings, I am disappointed with the Omron HEM 7140T1 Bluetooth Digital Blood Pressure Monitor. While the idea of a Bluetooth-enabled device with the convenience of tracking readings on a smartphone is appealing, the primary function of any blood pressure monitor should be accurate and reliable measurements.Firstly, the device consistently displays different readings every time it is used, with differences of up to 10 points. This inconsistency raises serious concerns about its accuracy and makes it challenging to trust the results. As someone who monitors their blood pressure regularly, having reliable readings is crucial for understanding my health and making informed decisions.I have also taken care to follow the manufacturer's instructions precisely, ensuring the cuff is appropriately positioned and my arm is at the correct level. Despite these efforts, the readings continue to fluctuate significantly. I have compared the device's readings with those taken at healthcare facilities, and the disparities are too substantial to ignore. This raises doubts about the overall reliability of the product.The Bluetooth functionality, which initially seemed like a useful feature, turns out to be more of a novelty than a practical benefit. While it's nice to see the readings on my phone and have the data stored in an app, these features lose their appeal when the readings themselves cannot be trusted. The app interface is also not the most user-friendly, and I have experienced occasional connectivity issues.On a positive note, the build quality of the device is decent, and the display is clear and easy to read. The cuff itself is comfortable to wear and fits well on my arm. However, these positives are overshadowed by the fundamental issue of unreliable and inconsistent readings.In conclusion, I cannot recommend the Omron HEM 7140T1 Bluetooth Digital Blood Pressure Monitor due to its lack of accurate readings and the significant variations observed between measurements. For a medical device that plays a vital role in monitoring one's health, this level of inconsistency is unacceptable. Until Omron addresses these issues and improves the product's accuracy and reliability, I would advise users to consider alternative options from more reputable brands. It's essential to prioritize the accuracy of blood pressure readings above all else when selecting a blood pressure monitor.

body: These electronic BP devices only give you an indicative reading so, it is always advisable to get a checkup done with a manual device.Bought for my family. Went for Omron thinking this was Japanese mfd but was in fact, made in Vietnam and China. After doing some extensive research online found there's a noticeable difference of opinion bet people who've bought devices mfd in Japan vs other countries. Unfortunately, the Japanese mfd models are out of stock or not sold in India. As we've been using Omron for years considered it reliable and upgraded from the 7120 to 7156 which has an electric adapter port and purchased an adapter separately from Omron.USAGE EXPERIENCE: After checking the readings have been disappointed with vastly different values in the same measurement for a normal healthy individual when compared to a manual BP device at the local clinic. Found glitches in the display and memory as well as date and time resetting automatically which is very irritating. In measurements, it was off the mark by 5 to 10 points when the margin for error is usually 1-3 points. These made me question the blind faith in Omron until now unfortunately, there is no better alternative avail in the market.CALIBRATE: Would therefore recommend anyone purchasing this to get it calibrated at the Omron service centre every 3-6 months and to check against a manual device before first use and at other times. These devices are very sensitive to handling.WRIST DEVICE: If you can afford it have a backup device such as the Omron wrist measurement device. Surprisingly, it was giving more reliable readings when compared to a manual BP device! Having both will give a better idea of the average.

They are to be monitored, to change medication as early as possible. Further it was very quick, as it recognises the BP during inflation itself, unlike my Dr Trust or Omron which pressurises first and recognise BP value during depressurization.I have purchased Omran HEM 7156T based it's design, features like 360 deg cuff. The cuff it self holds arm snugly, so no need to worry about loose or excess tight or requirment of other person help and feedback on accuracy at reviews (thanks for revieers).
